answer: To bid, a key needs timber, minted only when an anchor drawn at random from outside its cluster grades one of its delivered jobs as passing. Timber cannot be transferred. The spiral links keys that share host latency fingerprints or payout wallets. The k-th key linked to one operator must hold 3k timber before bidding. An honest newcomer earns 3 timber, about 3 GPU-hours of judged work. 100 clones need 15,150 timber, or 15,150 GPU-hours, which parallel hardware can spread but never shrink.
